newsitem.title: USA: Reno rejects outside counsel for citizenship probe.
newsitem.headline: Reno rejects outside counsel for citizenship probe.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno Wednesday rejected a request by five House Republicans for an independent investigation into the Clinton administration's programme to naturalise a record 1.3 million new citizens.

The Justice Department said Reno decided the information from the lawmakers did not provide "a specific and credible basis" that a person covered under the independent counsel law may have committed a federal crime.

Five members of the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee said in their request a month ago there had been "criminal fraud and abuse in connection with the Immigration and Naturalisation Service's (INS) Citzenship USA programme."

They charged Clinton administration officials had rushed the naturalisation programme for political gain, believing the new citizens would vote Democratic. Some of the immigrants had criminal records, which should have disqualified them.

The Republicans said the Citizenship USA programme had been "hijacked" by Vice President Al Gore's office "to produce a million new citizens by election day." They also charged there had been fraudulent testing of qualifications for citizenship.

The Justice Department said it reviewed allegations that President Clinton, Gore, Deputy Attorney General Jamie Gorelick and Assistant Attorney General Andrew Fois may be liable for a crime under the programme but found no evidence of wrongdoing. The allegations included obstructing congressional oversight and affecting an election through a federally funded programme.

Assistant Attorney General John Keeney said in a letter to the five Republicans that allegations that warrant further investigation involve low-ranking officials, who are not covered by the independent counsel law, and private firms.

He assured the lawmakers the Justice Department would continue to investigate the programme. "The criminal division is conducting a careful review of the issues identified in your letter," Kenney said.

Reno, whose future in Clinton's second term has yet to be resolved, last Friday rejected another request from five congressional Republicans for an independent counsel to investigate Democratic campaign fundraising.

Reacting to the congressional criticism, the Justice Department and the INS also announced plans to expand efforts to make sure that no individual becomes naturalised without the verified completion of an FBI fingerprint check.
The Justice Derpartment also said it would hire the accounting firm KPMG Peat Marwick to oversee an INS audit of naturalisation cases dating back to September 1995.
